Col to summit (grade: Class 3-4 / steep snow)
the Main/Lemah Three summit (7,512', the massif's true high point)

contradictions.why: descent and descent_text both describe reaching the summit from the col via an NW-ridge Class 2 finish and call it 'the true summit' — language that matches the neighboring Main Peak (Lemah Three) route, not Lemah Two. contradictions.fact: Does this route require leaving the trail near Williams Lake for an off-trail scramble via a class-4 notch, or stay on the trail all the way to Dutch Miller Gap with no detour?

claims.says: Approached via the PCT to Dutch Miller Gap, the route climbs about 500 feet of heather and rock steps...
reached by leaving the trail near Williams Lake for an off-trail scramble up the peak's east slope/northeast ridge, with a short but exposed class 4 notch as the crux below the summit

For this specific route: continue the standard Middle Fork Snoqualmie trail all the way up to Dutch Miller Gap, then climb directly above the gap onto the peak's northeast ridge/face — no cross-country detour into Summit Chief Valley needed.
There is no cross-country detour for this route: stay on the trail to the top.
The climbing starts DIRECTLY ABOVE THE GAP.

contradictions.why: The approach field's own opening sentences describe leaving the trail near Williams Lake for an off-trail scramble with a class-4-notch crux, then its last sentence reverses this and says to stay on the trail all the way to Dutch Miller Gap with no detour needed — directly self-contradictory. beta also names the PCT, which no other approach description for this route uses. The off-trail/Williams Lake/notch language matches this route's OWN 'Pete Lake and Summit Chief' alternate approach_variant, not the primary trail-only line.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach_variants[0] is explicitly marked primary:true and matches the last sentence of approach (stay on trail, climb directly above the gap); the Williams Lake/off-trail/class-4-notch language appears to be contamination from the route's own alternate 'Pete Lake and Summit Chief' approach_variant.

contradictions.fact: Approach: Williams-Lake/Dutch-Miller-Gap/class-4-notch boilerplate vs this route's own steel-bridge/cross-country-into-Summit-Chief-Valley turnoff

claims.says: Little Big Chief sits immediately southwest of the gap, reached by leaving the trail near Williams Lake for an off-trail scramble up the peak's east slope/northeast ridge, with a short but exposed class 4 notch as the crux below the summit.

For this specific route: leave the main Middle Fork Snoqualmie trail at a small steel bridge well before Dutch Miller Gap and cut cross-country south into Summit Chief Valley; the Northwest Face is visible on the east side of that valley, roughly 3 hours from the trailhead — a distinctly different final leg than the Northeast Face's direct ridge approach.

Do NOT walk the trail to Dutch Miller Gap. From the Middle Fork Snoqualmie road end, head up the valley on the trail until you reach a SMALL STEEL BRIDGE, well short of the gap — that bridge is the turnoff.

contradictions.why: The approach field's opening sentences (identical boilerplate shared with the Northeast Face route) describe reaching the peak past Dutch Miller Gap near Williams Lake via a class-4 notch, but this route's own last sentence and its approach_variants explicitly say NOT to walk to the gap at all — the turnoff is a steel bridge well short of it, into a different valley (Summit Chief Valley).
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach_variants[0] (this route's only listed variant) and the approach field's own last sentence agree: leave the trail at the steel bridge before the gap; the Williams Lake/Dutch-Miller-Gap/class-4-notch opening sentences are boilerplate copied from the Northeast Face route's approach text.
